why: An entry here is a claim that two names are the SAME IDEA, and that the lesson genuinely
teaches it under the other name. It is not a way to silence a gap.
Every entry states the name the lesson actually uses in `taughtAs`, and the gate re-checks
that this name really is present. An allowlist entry whose `taughtAs` has drifted out of the
lesson stops holding and the violation returns — so this file cannot rot into a mute list.
The common cause is that a catalog concept was named for the exam's phrasing while its lesson
was titled for the case it teaches through. That is legitimate. What is NOT legitimate is
adding an entry because the idea is 'sort of' covered: `SELCO affordability system` was
considered for this file and rejected, because the word 'afford' does not appear anywhere in
its own lesson and affordability is the whole point of the SELCO model.
